title: October 8, 1932: India's air force began with 5 pilots and 4 biplanes.

sources.text: MapsOfIndia - 8th October 1932: The Indian Air Force comes into being

caption:
October 8, 1932: India's air force began with 5 pilots and 4 biplanes.

It started as an auxiliary of the Royal Air Force, with five Cranwell-trained pilots and four Westland Wapiti biplanes based at Karachi. The first squadron wasn't raised until April 1933 - the institution existed on paper for months before it had a real unit to fly.

It was called the Royal Indian Air Force from 1945 until India became a republic in 1950, when it took its current name. October 8 has been observed as Indian Air Force Day every year since.

Five pilots and four borrowed-design biplanes in 1932 grew into a force defending a nation's entire airspace - a reminder that scale is built, not inherited.
